transport: RS-485, Modbus RTU — but as the bus MASTER, not as a slave.

models.name: MT50 remote meter (XTRA, TRIRON, TracerAN, Tracer BN — RJ45)
MT11 remote meter (DR N / DuoRacer series only — 3.81 mm 4-pin)
MT52 (the XTRA-N G3 generation's meter, named in the G3 manual)

refutedOnReview: REFUTED on the central claim. The dialect header asserts MT50/MT11/MT52 "share one register map", but no cited source contains a register map for any of the three, and the entry's own evidence text concedes "it is not a register map." These are Modbus masters (displays); EPEver publishes maps for the controllers (docs/epever-controller-protocol-a-b-series-v2.5.pdf, docs/epever-controller-protocol-b-series-v2.3.pdf),
gotchas: A second Modbus master on the bus. It will collide with the gateway's polling — tolerate the retries or unplug it. This is already in docs/DEVICES.md and docs/INVENTORY.md; it is repeated here because it is the single most likely cause of a driver that 'works on the bench and not at the cabin'.
MT50 does not support lithium battery parameters (stated in the XTRA-N manual's accessory table).
MT11 is DR-N-only by vendor statement; MT52 is the G3's meter. They are not interchangeable across product lines.
MT11 costs the shared 5 V rail 13 mA when on, 4 mA off — and on DR1206/2206/3206/2210/3210N that rail is shared with the AES refrigerator signal port.
